title: ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning
authors: Mohit Shridhar; Xingdi Yuan; Marc-Alexandre Côté; Yonatan Bisk; Adam Trischler; Matthew Hausknecht
version_status: arXiv preprint and ICLR 2021 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Whether text-policy agents transfer between abstract text and embodied environments
testing_method: benchmark testing; paired text/embodied environments
metrics: task success; transfer performance
main_findings: The abstract reports a shared task set linking text games and embodied household environments for interactive-agent training and evaluation.
limitations: Predates modern LLM agents; only abstract-level use in this review.

title: ScienceWorld: Is your Agent Smarter than a 5th Grader?
authors: Ruoyao Wang; Peter Jansen; Marc-Alexandre Côté; Prithviraj Ammanabrolu
version_status: arXiv preprint and EMNLP 2022 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate grounded scientific reasoning through interactive actions
testing_method: benchmark testing in simulated science environment
metrics: task success; subgoal/behavior analyses
main_findings: The abstract introduces an interactive elementary-science environment requiring observation, experimentation and multi-step action.
limitations: Older environment and not designed specifically for tool-using LLM agents; detailed claims not used without full read.

title: API-Bank: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Tool-Augmented LLMs
authors: Minghao Li; Yingxiu Zhao; Bowen Yu; Feifan Song; Hangyu Li; Haiyang Yu; Zhoujun Li; Fei Huang; Yongbin Li
version_status: arXiv preprint and EMNLP 2023 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate planning, API retrieval and API calling in multi-turn tool use
testing_method: benchmark testing with executable APIs
metrics: API selection/call correctness; response quality
main_findings: The abstract presents an executable tool-use benchmark and tool-augmented model baseline covering planning, retrieval and calling.
limitations: Primarily abstract-level evidence here; narrower and less stateful than later interactive benchmarks.

title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
authors: Xiang Deng; Yu Gu; Boyuan Zheng; Shijie Chen; Samuel Stevens; Boshi Wang; Huan Sun; Yu Su
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2023 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Measure cross-website and cross-domain generalization of web action prediction
testing_method: offline benchmark from real websites
metrics: element selection; action prediction; task-level performance
main_findings: The abstract introduces diverse real-world website tasks and emphasizes generalization to unseen websites and domains.
limitations: Offline traces do not reproduce the full dynamics and side effects of live browser execution; detailed results not used.

title: InterCode: Standardizing and Benchmarking Interactive Coding with Execution Feedback
authors: John Yang; Akshara Prabhakar; Karthik Narasimhan; Shunyu Yao
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2023 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate iterative code/action generation with execution feedback
testing_method: interactive execution benchmark
metrics: task success; interaction efficiency
main_findings: The abstract standardizes interactive coding environments in which agents receive execution feedback and iteratively revise actions.
limitations: Not a repository-level software-engineering agent benchmark; only abstract-level evidence used.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
authors: Shuyan Zhou; Frank F. Xu; Hao Zhu; Xuhui Zhou; Robert Lo; Abishek Sridhar; Xianyi Cheng; Tianyue Ou; Yonatan Bisk; Daniel Fried; Uri Alon; Graham Neubig
version_status: arXiv preprint and ICLR 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate autonomous completion of realistic, long-horizon web tasks
testing_method: self-hosted interactive benchmark; executable functional oracle
metrics: task success; per-site/category success
main_findings: Self-hosted websites and execution-based evaluators expose a large human–agent gap and substantial cross-task instability in the evaluated model snapshot.
limitations: Website/state maintenance is expensive; functional end-state checks can miss unsafe intermediate behavior.

title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
authors: Yujia Qin; Shihao Liang; Yining Ye; Kunlun Zhu; Lan Yan; Yaxi Lu; Yankai Lin; Xin Cong; Xiangru Tang; Bill Qian; Sihan Zhao; Lauren Hong; Runchu Tian; Ruobing Xie; Jie Zhou; Mark Gerstein; Dahai Li; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun
version_status: arXiv preprint and ICLR 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Scale API retrieval, planning and multi-step execution over real-world tools
testing_method: ToolBench benchmark; depth-first decision-tree data generation; automatic evaluator
metrics: pass rate; win rate; API retrieval/selection performance
main_findings: The work establishes a large tool corpus and multi-step evaluation pipeline; the detailed note separates model training contribution from benchmark validity and API instability.
limitations: Live APIs, LLM evaluators and data-generation bias limit longitudinal reproducibility.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
authors: Xiao Liu; Hao Yu; Hanchen Zhang; Yifan Xu; Xuanyu Lei; Hanyu Lai; Yu Gu; Hangliang Ding; Kaiwen Men; Kejuan Yang; Shudan Zhang; Xiang Deng; Aohan Zeng; Zhengxiao Du; Chenhui Zhang; Sheng Shen; Tianjun Zhang; Yu Su; Huan Sun; Minlie Huang; Yuxiao Dong; Jie Tang
version_status: arXiv preprint and ICLR 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate LLM agents across heterogeneous interactive environments and diagnose long-trajectory failures
testing_method: multi-environment benchmark; trajectory failure taxonomy
metrics: weighted overall score; task success; failure types; rounds/tokens
main_findings: Across eight environments, final score hides invalid-action, format, context-limit and task-limit failures; repeated-response loops dominate many task-limit traces.
limitations: Environment aggregation and model/API snapshots limit comparability; not a safety benchmark.

title: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
authors: Yangjun Ruan; Honghua Dong; Andrew Wang; Silviu Pitis; Yongchao Zhou; Jimmy Ba; Yann Dubois; Chris J. Maddison; Tatsunori Hashimoto
version_status: arXiv preprint and ICLR 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Discover realistic tool-agent risks without executing dangerous real tools
testing_method: LM-emulated sandbox; adversarial scenario generation; automated safety evaluator
metrics: risk occurrence; evaluator precision/recall; human confirmation
main_findings: Scalable emulation can surface high-risk failures and support adversarial testing, but confirmed realism and judge calibration must be reported separately.
limitations: Simulation-to-real gap; LM simulator and evaluator errors; threat model emphasizes underspecified instructions.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
authors: Carlos E. Jimenez; John Yang; Alexander Wettig; Shunyu Yao; Kexin Pei; Ofir Press; Karthik Narasimhan
version_status: arXiv preprint and ICLR 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate repository-level issue resolution against real tests
testing_method: execution-based benchmark; fail-to-pass and regression tests
metrics: percentage resolved; patch application; test outcomes
main_findings: Repository execution provides a stronger oracle than text similarity and reveals localization/context bottlenecks in the evaluated baselines.
limitations: Python-only original set; tests are incomplete quality oracles; static tasks face contamination and environment drift.

title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
authors: Grégoire Mialon; Clémentine Fourrier; Craig Swift; Thomas Wolf; Yann LeCun; Thomas Scialom
version_status: arXiv preprint and ICLR 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate real-world questions requiring reasoning, multimodality, browsing and tools
testing_method: human-authored benchmark with exact/normalized answers and difficulty levels
metrics: accuracy by level; human–model gap
main_findings: The benchmark exposes a large gap on multi-step Level-3 tasks; the paper's manually selected plugin result is an oracle-style estimate rather than a fully reproducible agent configuration.
limitations: Exact-answer grading misses process quality; tool/plugin setup and changing web sources constrain reproducibility.

title: Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
authors: Jingwei Yi; Yueqi Xie; Bin Zhu; Emre Kiciman; Guangzhong Sun; Xing Xie; Fangzhao Wu
version_status: 2023 arXiv preprint and KDD 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Benchmark indirect prompt injection and compare defenses
testing_method: adversarial benchmark; attack/defense evaluation
metrics: attack success; utility/defense performance
main_findings: The abstract establishes a benchmark for indirect prompt injection delivered through external content and evaluates defense strategies.
limitations: Includes non-agent LLM settings and is used only at abstract level here.

title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
authors: Chang Ma; Junlei Zhang; Zhihao Zhu; Cheng Yang; Yujiu Yang; Yaohui Jin; Zhenzhong Lan; Lingpeng Kong; Junxian He
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Make agent evaluation progress-aware and diagnostically interpretable
testing_method: multi-benchmark board; human-authored subgoals; trajectory visualization
metrics: task success; progress rate; grounding and skill indicators
main_findings: Progress rate strongly agrees with sampled human judgments and exposes partial completion hidden by binary success; the paper has a one-instance internal count discrepancy.
limitations: Manual subgoal design is costly; aggregation across heterogeneous environments remains sensitive to task composition.

title: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visual Web Tasks
authors: Jing Yu Koh; Robert Lo; Lawrence Jang; Vikram Duvvur; Ming Lim; Po-Yu Huang; Graham Neubig; Shuyan Zhou; Ruslan Salakhutdinov; Daniel Fried
version_status: arXiv preprint and ACL 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate visually grounded actions on realistic websites
testing_method: interactive benchmark; functional evaluators; multimodal observations
metrics: task success; category performance; human–agent gap
main_findings: Visual grounding plus long-horizon control remains difficult; traces reveal premature stopping, loops and accumulated input errors in addition to perception failures.
limitations: Self-hosted sites and model updates complicate maintenance; functional oracle under-observes unsafe processes.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
authors: Qiusi Zhan; Zhixiang Liang; Zifan Ying; Daniel Kang
version_status: arXiv preprint and Findings of ACL 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Measure indirect prompt injection delivered through tool responses
testing_method: benchmark testing; adversarial injection; defense comparison
metrics: attack success; utility; defense trade-off
main_findings: The benchmark systematically pairs user tasks, tools and attacker goals, showing that tool-return injections can redirect actions; exact conclusions are bounded to the tested attacks and models.
limitations: Mostly static attack templates; tool simulation and evaluator assumptions constrain external validity.

title: StableToolBench: Towards Stable Large-Scale Benchmarking on Tool Learning of Large Language Models
authors: Zhicheng Guo; Sijie Cheng; Hao Wang; Shihao Liang; Yujia Qin; Peng Li; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun; Yang Liu
version_status: arXiv preprint and Findings of ACL 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Reduce instability from changing and unavailable real APIs in large-scale tool evaluation
testing_method: virtual API system; stable benchmark; evaluator refinement
metrics: pass/win rates; API execution stability
main_findings: The abstract proposes stable virtualized APIs and revised evaluation to improve reproducibility of ToolBench-style testing.
limitations: Only abstract read; virtualization may reduce real-world fidelity and detailed trade-offs are not asserted.

title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
authors: Tianbao Xie; Danyang Zhang; Jixuan Chen; Xiaochuan Li; Siheng Zhao; Ruisheng Cao; Toh Jing Hua; Zhoujun Cheng; Dongchan Shin; Fangyu Lei; Yitao Liu; Yiheng Xu; Shuyan Zhou; Silvio Savarese; Caiming Xiong; Victor Zhong; Tao Yu
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate open-ended computer tasks in real operating systems
testing_method: VM-based interactive benchmark; task-specific execution evaluators; perturbation tests
metrics: task success; perturbation robustness; human–agent gap
main_findings: Real VM execution reveals a very large human–agent gap and strong sensitivity to window layout and visual clutter, separating environment-control robustness from pure reasoning.
limitations: VM setup is expensive; apps and OS versions drift; task-specific evaluators require maintenance.

title: Testing and Understanding Erroneous Planning in LLM Agents through Synthesized User Inputs
authors: Zhenlan Ji; Daoyuan Wu; Pingchuan Ma; Zongjie Li; Shuai Wang
version_status: arXiv preprint; no formal version verified
research_problem: Automatically expose erroneous multi-action plans
testing_method: DSL-based test synthesis; constraint solving; mock tools; mutation analysis
metrics: constraint violation; error type; success vs action length; generation cost
main_findings: Constraint-driven input synthesis exposes ordering, omission and parameter errors and supports precise, low-cost planning oracles.
limitations: Synthetic independent actions, mock tools, limited models/frameworks and simplified dependencies restrict external validity.

title: AndroidWorld: A Dynamic Benchmarking Environment for Autonomous Agents
authors: Christopher Rawles; Sarah Clinckemaillie; Yifan Chang; Jonathan Waltz; Gabrielle Lau; Marybeth Fair; Alice Li; William Bishop; Wei Li; Folawiyo Campbell-Ajala; Daniel Toyama; Robert Berry; Divya Tyamagundlu; Timothy Lillicrap; Oriana Riva
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and ICLR 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate autonomous agents in reproducible Android app tasks
testing_method: dynamic emulator benchmark; programmatic task generation and evaluators
metrics: task success; generalization across task instances
main_findings: The abstract introduces a dynamic Android environment with programmatic task generation and reproducible state-based evaluation.
limitations: Only abstract read; mobile-emulator maintenance and app/version coverage need further verification.

title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
authors: Shunyu Yao; Noah Shinn; Pedram Razavi; Karthik Narasimhan
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and ICLR 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate policy-compliant tool use with users and stateful databases; measure repeated reliability
testing_method: POMDP interaction; executable end-state oracle; repeated trials
metrics: task success; pass^k; error categories; hallucinated identifiers; cost
main_findings: Single-run success substantially overstates repeated reliability; failures split across parameters/facts, policy decisions and partial compound tasks.
limitations: LLM user simulator errors; terminal-state oracle misses process policy violations; two domains and closed APIs limit generalization.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
authors: Edoardo Debenedetti; Jie Zhang; Mislav Balunović; Luca Beurer-Kellner; Marc Fischer; Florian Tramèr
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Jointly evaluate normal utility and indirect prompt-injection security in stateful tools
testing_method: dynamic environment; deterministic utility/security checks; adaptive attacks
metrics: benign utility; utility under attack; targeted ASR
main_findings: Environment-state oracles expose a utility–security trade-off and show that attack wording, placement and defense adaptation materially change results.
limitations: Synthetic applications; hand-built tasks; limited long-term/multimodal coverage; internal 70/74 tool-count inconsistency.

title: AI Agents That Matter
authors: Sayash Kapoor; Benedikt Stroebl; Zachary S. Siegel; Nitya Nadgir; Arvind Narayanan
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and TMLR 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Improve statistical, cost-aware and contamination-aware evaluation of agents
testing_method: methodological analysis; cost–accuracy comparison; reproducibility audit
metrics: accuracy with uncertainty; cost; Pareto efficiency; contamination risk
benchmark_or_dataset: multiple agent benchmarks and case studies
main_findings: The paper argues that accuracy-only leaderboards, single runs, weak baselines and benchmark overfitting can make agent improvements misleading; cost and uncertainty must be first-class.
limitations: Meta-evaluation covers selected systems and rapidly changing APIs; not itself a universal benchmark.

title: WorkArena++: Towards Compositional Planning and Reasoning-based Common Knowledge Work Tasks
authors: Léo Boisvert; Megh Thakkar; Maxime Gasse; Massimo Caccia; Thibault Le Sellier de Chezelles; Quentin Cappart; Nicolas Chapados; Alexandre Lacoste; Alexandre Drouin
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate compositional common-knowledge work in enterprise software
testing_method: interactive benchmark; compositional tasks and execution evaluators
metrics: task success; compositional/generalization analyses
main_findings: The abstract extends enterprise web testing to compositional tasks requiring planning and reasoning across common workflows.
limitations: Only abstract read; relies on a specific enterprise platform and expensive maintained environment.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
authors: Zhaorun Chen; Zhen Xiang; Chaowei Xiao; Dawn Song; Bo Li
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Test targeted backdoors introduced through agent memory or knowledge bases
testing_method: poisoning/red-team benchmark
metrics: attack success; benign utility/stealth
main_findings: The abstract shows that poisoned long-term memory or retrieval knowledge can trigger targeted malicious agent behavior while aiming to preserve benign behavior.
limitations: Only abstract read; threat assumptions and deployment realism are not used for detailed conclusions.

title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
authors: Harsh Trivedi; Tushar Khot; Mareike Hartmann; Ruskin Manku; Vinty Dong; Edward Li; Shashank Gupta; Ashish Sabharwal; Niranjan Balasubramanian
version_status: arXiv preprint and ACL 2024 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate code-generating agents over interconnected applications and mutable databases
testing_method: sandboxed app world; executable tests; expected and allowed state changes
metrics: task/requirement success; state-change correctness; collateral damage
main_findings: Database-difference oracles test both intended effects and unauthorized collateral changes, offering a strong model for enterprise workflow QA.
limitations: Synthetic apps and generated data differ from production; execution environments and evaluator coverage require maintenance.

title: BadRobot: Jailbreaking Embodied LLM Agents in the Physical World
authors: Hangtao Zhang; Chenyu Zhu; Xianlong Wang; Ziqi Zhou; Changgan Yin; Minghui Li; Lulu Xue; Yichen Wang; Shengshan Hu; Aishan Liu; Peijin Guo; Leo Yu Zhang
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and ICLR 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Measure whether language-to-action agents execute unsafe physical instructions
testing_method: embodied jailbreaking benchmark; action-level harmfulness evaluation
metrics: attack success/harmfulness; task execution; cross-model comparisons
main_findings: Language safety does not automatically transfer to the physical action layer; decomposition and action grounding create additional attack surfaces.
limitations: Selected robots/tasks and simulated or lab settings limit generalization; safety judge and physical-risk realism require care.

title: Breaking Agents: Compromising Autonomous LLM Agents Through Malfunction Amplification
authors: Boyang Zhang; Yicong Tan; Yun Shen; Ahmed Salem; Michael Backes; Savvas Zannettou; Yang Zhang
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and EMNLP 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Amplify ordinary malfunction patterns into attacks against autonomous agents
testing_method: adversarial testing; malfunction amplification
metrics: attack success; task utility
main_findings: The abstract frames ordinary agent failure modes as exploitable attack primitives and evaluates compromise across autonomous-agent settings.
limitations: Only abstract read; detailed attack assumptions and model-specific results are not used.

title: ToolSandbox: A Stateful, Conversational, Interactive Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Tool Use Capabilities
authors: Jiarui Lu; Thomas Holleis; Yizhe Zhang; Bernhard Aumayer; Feng Nan; Haoping Bai; Shuang Ma; Shen Ma; Mengyu Li; Guoli Yin; Zirui Wang; Ruoming Pang
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and Findings of NAACL 2025 formal version; formal version preferred; author-name conflict resolved in favor of formal metadata
research_problem: Evaluate multi-turn tool use with implicit state dependencies and flexible valid trajectories
testing_method: state snapshots; milestone/minefield DAG; tool-schema perturbation; user simulation
metrics: trajectory score; scenario-category score; simulator error rates
main_findings: Dynamic milestone and minefield checks accept equivalent paths while detecting missing prerequisites and forbidden states; tool metadata perturbations expose interface brittleness.
limitations: Manual oracle construction; simulator errors; limited authentication, async and external-API coverage.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
authors: Hanrong Zhang; Jingyuan Huang; Kai Mei; Yifei Yao; Zhenting Wang; Chenlu Zhan; Hongwei Wang; Yongfeng Zhang
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and ICLR 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Systematize attacks, defenses and evaluation dimensions for LLM agents
testing_method: security benchmark across attacks and defenses
metrics: attack success; utility; defense effectiveness
main_findings: The abstract presents a unified benchmark and taxonomy spanning multiple agent attacks and defenses.
limitations: Only abstract read; aggregate results depend on selected agents, attacks and defenses.

title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
authors: Maksym Andriushchenko; Alexandra Souly; Mateusz Dziemian; Derek Duenas; Maxwell Lin; Justin Wang; Dan Hendrycks; Andy Zou; Zico Kolter; Matt Fredrikson; Yarin Gal; Xander Davies
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and ICLR 2025 formal version; formal version has 12 authors and is preferred
research_problem: Evaluate multi-step harmful tool behavior and jailbreak susceptibility
testing_method: harmful-task benchmark; tool environment; jailbreak evaluation
metrics: harmful task success; refusal/utility; attack transfer
main_findings: Agentic harmfulness requires evaluating whether multi-step tool actions actually achieve a harmful goal, not merely whether text is unsafe.
limitations: Synthetic tools/tasks and evaluator calibration limit real-world inference; model snapshots age quickly.

title: Agent-as-a-Judge: Evaluate Agents with Agents
authors: Mingchen Zhuge; Changsheng Zhao; Dylan R. Ashley; Wenyi Wang; Dmitrii Khizbullin; Yunyang Xiong; Zechun Liu; Ernie Chang; Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi; Yuandong Tian; Yangyang Shi; Vikas Chandra; Jürgen Schmidhuber
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and ICML 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Evaluate agents using an evaluator that can inspect and act in the same workspace
testing_method: agentic evaluator; hierarchical requirements; human comparison
metrics: agreement/accuracy; requirement-level feedback; time and cost
main_findings: An evaluator agent can inspect artifacts and provide process-level evidence more effectively than a single-turn judge in the studied code-generation setting, but its own planning and memory remain error sources.
limitations: Small domain-specific benchmark; evaluator-agent errors can cascade; closed model/version dependence.

title: AgentOps: Enabling Observability of LLM Agents
authors: Liming Dong; Qinghua Lu; Liming Zhu
version_status: arXiv preprint; no formal version verified
research_problem: Define agent-specific observability artifacts and compare current tools
testing_method: multivocal/tool mapping study; taxonomy construction
metrics: feature coverage across 17 tools
main_findings: The study argues that output-only monitoring is insufficient and organizes spans for agents, plans, reasoning, tools, evaluation and guardrails.
limitations: Search limited to selected queries/pages and fast-changing tool documentation; taxonomy not empirically validated as a detector.

title: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research
authors: Thibault Le Sellier de Chezelles; Maxime Gasse; Alexandre Lacoste; Massimo Caccia; Alexandre Drouin; Léo Boisvert; Megh Thakkar; Tom Marty; Rim Assouel; Sahar Omidi Shayegan; Lawrence Keunho Jang; Xing Han Lù; Ori Yoran; Dehan Kong; Frank F. Xu; Siva Reddy; Graham Neubig; Quentin Cappart; Russ Salakhutdinov; Nicolas Chapados
version_status: 2024 arXiv preprint and TMLR 2025 formal version; formal author order preferred
research_problem: Unify fragmented web benchmarks, action/observation spaces and experiment management
testing_method: standardized harness; six-benchmark comparative experiment
metrics: task success; cross-benchmark/model comparison; experiment metadata
main_findings: A common harness reduces implementation confounds and enables broader cross-benchmark comparison, while results still show strong environment/model interaction.
limitations: Unified interface cannot eliminate benchmark-specific oracle quality, site drift or infrastructure cost.

title: SafeAgentBench: A Benchmark for Safe Task Planning of Embodied LLM Agents
authors: Sheng Yin; Xianghe Pang; Yuanzhuo Ding; Menglan Chen; Yutong Bi; Yichen Xiong; Wenhao Huang; Zhen Xiang; Jing Shao; Siheng Chen
version_status: arXiv preprint; an ICLR 2026 review page was not treated as proof of formal publication
research_problem: Evaluate whether plans remain safe while completing embodied tasks
testing_method: safe-planning benchmark; hazard and utility evaluation
metrics: task success; safety violation; plan quality
main_findings: The benchmark separates successful task planning from unsafe physical actions and supports analysis of safety–utility trade-offs.
limitations: Preprint evidence; simulated tasks and safety labeling may not capture real-world severity.

title: Agent-SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of LLM Agents
authors: Zhexin Zhang; Shiyao Cui; Yida Lu; Jingzhuo Zhou; Junxiao Yang; Hongning Wang; Minlie Huang
version_status: arXiv preprint; later workshop listing does not replace publication identity used here
research_problem: Evaluate diverse agent safety risks across environments and failure categories
testing_method: multi-category safety benchmark
metrics: safe completion; risk-category performance; utility
main_findings: The benchmark broadens agent safety beyond refusal to risks caused by planning, tool calls and environment interaction.
limitations: Preprint; benchmark coverage, evaluator choices and rapidly changing agent implementations limit durability.

title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
authors: Qiusi Zhan; Richard Fang; Henil Shalin Panchal; Daniel Kang
version_status: arXiv preprint and Findings of NAACL 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Test whether prompt-injection defenses survive attacks adapted to the defense
testing_method: adaptive adversarial evaluation
metrics: adaptive attack success; defense utility
main_findings: The abstract reports that defenses appearing effective under static attacks can fail when the attacker adapts to the defense.
limitations: Only abstract read; detailed attack budget and defense-specific numbers are not used.

title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM agents
authors: Kunlun Zhu; Hongyi Du; Zhaochen Hong; Xiaocheng Yang; Shuyi Guo; Zhe Wang; Zhenhailong Wang; Cheng Qian; Xiangru Tang; Heng Ji; Jiaxuan You
version_status: arXiv preprint and ACL 2025 formal version; formal metadata preferred
research_problem: Evaluate task outcomes plus collaboration and competition under different coordination topologies
testing_method: interactive scenarios; milestone KPIs; topology and planning ablations
metrics: task score; milestone achievement; coordination/competition indicators
main_findings: Process-oriented milestone metrics and topology comparisons show that team success alone is insufficient to characterize coordination quality.
limitations: Scenario and protocol coverage is finite; LLM-driven roles and evaluators can introduce correlated errors.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
authors: Mert Cemri; Melissa Z. Pan; Shuyi Yang; Lakshya A. Agrawal; Bhavya Chopra; Rishabh Tiwari; Kurt Keutzer; Aditya Parameswaran; Dan Klein; Kannan Ramchandran; Matei Zaharia; Joseph E. Gonzalez; Ion Stoica
version_status: arXiv preprint and NeurIPS 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Develop a failure taxonomy and analyze where multi-agent workflows break
testing_method: trajectory annotation and failure taxonomy across MAS traces
metrics: failure-category frequency; task success; propagation patterns
main_findings: The abstract identifies recurring failures in coordination, verification and communication and motivates trajectory-level root-cause analysis.
limitations: Only abstract read; taxonomy coverage and annotator agreement require full-text confirmation before detailed use.

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
authors: Haoyu Wang; Christopher M. Poskitt; Jun Sun
version_status: 2025 arXiv preprint; ICSE 2026 acceptance verified; DOI not yet verified
research_problem: Express and enforce customizable safety and reliability policies before actions execute
testing_method: DSL rules; runtime predicates; action blocking
metrics: policy conformance; harmful-action blocking; overhead; utility
main_findings: The abstract and verified paper identity present a runtime policy layer that checks predicates and blocks disallowed actions across agent settings.
limitations: No verified DOI yet; rule coverage is limited by what can be expressed and observed; detailed results not used here without a dedicated note.
openalex_status: exact preprint and acceptance record verified

title: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
authors: Xing Han Lù; Amirhossein Kazemnejad; Nicholas Meade; Arkil Patel; Dongchan Shin; Alejandra Zambrano; Karolina Stańczak; Peter Shaw; Christopher J. Pal; Siva Reddy
version_status: arXiv preprint and COLM 2025 formal version; formal version preferred
research_problem: Measure how accurately rules and LLM judges classify agent trajectory success, side effects and repetition
testing_method: expert-labeled meta-evaluation; rule and judge comparison
metrics: precision; recall; F1; evaluator-induced success-rate bias
main_findings: No tested judge is uniformly best; rules are precise but miss flexible success paths, while LLM judges tend to over-credit plausible self-reports.
limitations: Five web benchmarks and four agent families; expert labels and dynamic websites add noise; judge cost/stability not fully covered.

title: Agent-Testing Agent: A Meta-Agent for Automated Testing and Evaluation of Conversational AI Agents
authors: Sameer Komoravolu; Khalil Mrini
version_status: formal EACL 2026 version
research_problem: Automate adaptive adversarial test generation for an agent under test
testing_method: meta-agent; code analysis; persona tests; judge-feedback adaptation
metrics: failure diversity; severity; time
main_findings: Combines evidence about the AUT with feedback-driven test generation and produces quantitative results plus bug reports.
limitations: Two studied applications and reliance on LLM-as-a-Judge limit broad generalization.

title: SIRAJ: Diverse and Efficient Red-Teaming for LLM Agents via Distilled Structured Reasoning
authors: Kaiwen Zhou; Ahmed Elgohary; A S M Iftekhar; Amin Saied
version_status: formal Findings EACL 2026 version
research_problem: Generate diverse and adaptive safety tests at lower red-team cost
testing_method: risk seed generation; trajectory-feedback attack refinement; reasoning distillation
metrics: risk and trajectory coverage; attack success; cost
